claim: Hedy Lamarr has been rediscovered as the mother of modern-day wi-fi technology.

evidence.quote: the celebrated screen siren Hedy Lamarr has been rediscovered. But not so much for her extraordinary beauty or even her various iconic film roles (“Delilah,” anyone?), but, remarkably, as the mother of modern-day wi-fi technology.

notes: Characterization by a Library of Congress blog author; relevant to the IHH page claim about Wi-Fi.

claim: Hedy Lamarr's 1942 invention of spread-spectrum technology has served, largely, as the basis for such commonplace conveniences as Bluetooth and cellphones.

evidence.quote: And her 1942 invention of “spread-spectrum” technology (US Patent #2,292,387; registered on August 11, 1942, under Lamarr’s then-married name of Hedy Kiesler Marke) has served, largely, as the basis for a host of such now commonplace conveniences as Bluetooth and cellphones.
the celebrated screen siren Hedy Lamarr has been rediscovered

notes: Supports the Bluetooth part of the IHH page legacy claim; the post names cellphones, not Wi-Fi, in this sentence.

claim: In 1940, Hedy Lamarr was the wife of Gene Markey.
